## Summary

The 2D axis-based reductions for `BaseMaskedArray` were broken in two ways: `min`/`max` flattened the array (returning a scalar) for any axis, and every reduction returned a single scalar `pd.NA` under `skipna=False` on 2D input instead of a per-slice array. `mean`/`var`/`std`/`sum` already worked for `skipna=True, axis=0`.

I made targeted changes in two source files (no test files touched):

### `pandas/core/array_algos/masked_reductions.py`
- **`_reductions`** (sum/prod/mean/var/std): the `skipna=False` early scalar-`NA` return now only fires when the result is genuinely scalar (`axis is None or ndim == 1`). For a 2D axis reduction it computes over the raw values with `where=~mask`, letting the caller mask any slice containing an NA.
- **`_minmax`**: added a 2D-axis branch. Masked entries are filled with the reduction's identity (dtype max for `min`, dtype min for `max`; `±inf` for floats; handles bool) via a new `_minmax_fill_value` helper, so they never win the per-slice min/max. All-NA slices get masked afterward. The `skipna=False` scalar short-circuit is likewise gated to scalar results.
- **`mean`/`var`/`std`**: the `mask.all()` short-circuit is gated to scalar results so a fully-masked 2D array still returns an array; `mean` now suppresses the empty-slice `RuntimeWarning` like `var`/`std`.

### `pandas/core/arrays/masked.py`
- **`_wrap_min_count_reduction_result`**: the `min_count == 0` "mask nothing" fast path now also requires `skipna` to be true. Under `skipna=False` it falls through to `_wrap_reduction_result`, which masks columns/rows containing any NA via `self._mask.any(axis=axis)`. This fixes `sum`/`prod` incorrectly returning valid values for NA-containing columns.

The wrapping logic in `_wrap_reduction_result` (`mask.all(axis)` for skipna, `mask.any(axis)` otherwise) already produced correct NA placement and preserved dtype (`IntegerArray`/`FloatingArray`) once the reduction functions returned proper ndarrays.
